title: Does the Bitcoin white paper say what people say it says?
done_when: Every statement has a verdict agreed by two different vendors, each with a quote from the paper.

statement/*.brief: Statement {n} about the Bitcoin white paper: {claim.text} The paper is Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, by Satoshi Nakamoto, 2008, nine pages, found by its title anywhere. Read it and return whether the paper says this, with a quote of at most 25 words from the paper as evidence.

claims.text: The paper proposes a solution to the double-spending problem that needs no trusted third party.
The paper defines an electronic coin as a chain of digital signatures.
The paper says proof-of-work amounts to one vote per IP address.
The paper says the proof-of-work difficulty is fixed when the network starts and never changes.
The paper says nodes always consider the longest chain to be the correct one.
The paper says the first transaction in a block creates new coins owned by the block's creator.
The paper says that once a predetermined number of coins have entered circulation, the incentive can come entirely from transaction fees.
The paper says a block header with no transactions would be about 80 bytes.
The paper says a payment can be verified only by running a full network node.
The paper recommends using a new key pair for each transaction.
The paper says an attacker with more computing power than the honest nodes could create coins out of thin air.
The paper models the race between the honest chain and an attacker's chain as a Binomial Random Walk.
The paper says a transaction normally has at most two outputs, one for the payment and one for the change.
The paper says nodes must be identified to one another so that messages can be routed.
The paper says blocks are generated every ten minutes.
The paper cites Adam Back's Hashcash as the model for its proof-of-work.
